description_en: The Aśoka Stūpa North is one of 5stūpasbelieved to have been built by King Aśoka in the 3rd century BCE, although, there is no evidence that King Aśoka ever visited the Kathmandu Valley. There is one Asoka stupa in the center of Patan and the other four are placed in cardinal directions on what had been the periphery of the ancient city. Thestūpasare collectively called Pyãḥthūra in Newari. Thestūpasin the east, west, north and south are named Tetāthūra, Pūcvathūra, Ībahīthūra and Lagãthūra, respectively. It is quite possible that these stūpas represent some of the oldest types of structures in the Valley, predating the Mauryan Empire.Thestuparesembles the Svayambhū Mahācaitya. Statues of the four Buddhas can be found in the four niches of thevedi,whilst Akṣobhya are in the eastern and southern niches. Meanwhile, the western and northern niches contain images of Amitābha. In the northern niche, this Amitābha image also has an umbrella of seven serpents. Images of Tārā can be found in the south-east, south-west, north-west and north-east niches.To the south-east of the Ibahī Stūpa there is a shrine of Budhavāra deity. The priest of thestūpa(Devaratna Śākya, 48), however, claims that the deity inside the shrine is Vairocana, as it is found in Svayambhū Mahācaitya. Unfortunately, the image is broken so it is difficult to tell whether it depicts Vairocana or not. Two statues of lions can be found in front of the image.Above thekumbhaof thestūpais aharmikā. The two eyes painted on each side of theharmikāare calledvajradṛṣṭi. Between the eyes, there is a depiction of the small curl of hair that grows between eyebrows. This hair is calledūrṇā,and here it curls towards the right. Above theharmikāthere are 13 circles symbolizing 13bhuvanas, as well asāmalaka,bāymvaḥand a pinnacle.Surrounding thestūpastructure are fixedmānes. Inside thestūpacourtyard aredharmadhātumaṇdalas, eightvajradhātucaityasand twośikharakūṭacaityas. Moreover, there is a long stone considered as anāga, a shrine of Sarasvatī, and a pillar used to light a lamp.Over time dramatic changes took place: a historic photograph from the 1920s depicts the earthen mound covered by grass and a steppedharmikā, most likely built of brick and whitewashed with lime. The central wooden pillar extends from theharmikāwith the finial missing, which would indicate that thestūpawas under restoration at that time. 50 years later, in ca. 1973, the photograph from Pruscha's inventory, shows the earthen mound covered with white-washed plaster and a completely rebuiltharmikāand finial.
description_ne: ललितपुरको चार दिशामा चार ठूला स्तूप रहेका छन्- पूर्वमा तेता स्तूप, दक्षिणमा लगनखेल स्तूप, पश्चिममा पुल्चोक स्तूप र उत्तरमा ईबही स्तूप । ईशापूर्व तेस्रो शताब्दीमा अथवा चौधौँ किराती राजा स्थुंकोको पालामा भारतका सम्राट् अशोक नेपालमा आएका थिए र उनले नै ललितपुरको चार दिशामा चार स्तूप बनाए भन्ने मानिन्छ र त्यसैले ती स्तूपहरूलाई अशोक स्तूप भनिन्छ । तर यस कुरालाई प्रमाणित गर्ने ऐतिहासिक स्रोतको अभाव छ ।समयक्रमसँगै ईबही स्तूपमा धेरै परिवर्तन आइसकेका छन्, धेरै कलाकृति थपिएका छन्, केही मौलिक कलाकृति परिवर्तित अवस्थामा छन् । अहिले यस स्तूपको प्रवेशद्वार आधुनिक शैलीले प्लाष्टर गरी बनाइएको छ । ढोकामा दायाँ-बायाँ चन्द्र-सूर्य सहित अष्टमङ्गल राखिएका छन् । ढोकामाथि तीनवटा चैत्यलाई गजूरको रूपमा राखिएको छ । ढोकाबाट छिरेपछि विशाल स्तूप देख्न सकिन्छ । यो स्तूपको शैली स्वयम्भू महाचैत्यको शैलीसँग धेरै मिल्छ । स्तूपको कुम्भमा प्लाष्टर गरी चून पोतिएको छ । स्तूपको वेदिकामा चार दिशामा चार बुद्ध राखिएका छन्,  तर चैत्यको कुन दिशामा कुन बुद्ध रहने भन्ने शास्त्रीय नियम यहाँ पालन भएको देखिँदैन । पूर्वमा अक्षोभ्यलाई स्तूपको मुख्य देवताको रूपमा स्थापना गरिएको छ । त्यस्तै दक्षिणमा पनि अक्षोभ्य, पश्चिममा अमिताभ र उत्तरमा सप्तनागको छत्र ओढेका अमिताभ बुद्ध राखिएका छन् । दक्षिण-पूर्व, दक्षिण-पश्चिम, उत्तर-पश्चिम र उत्तर-पूर्व दिशामा ताराहरू राखिएका छन् । स्तूपको पूर्व-दक्षिण दिशामा बुधबार देवता स्थापना गरिएको छ । स्तूपका पूजारी यसलाई बुधबार देवता नभई स्वयम्भू महाचैत्यमा जस्तै वैरोचन राखिएको हो भनी दावी गर्छन् (देवरत्न शाक्य, ४८, पूजारी) । देवताको हात भाँचिएकोले वैरोचन बुद्ध हुन् वा होइनन् भन्न सकिने अवस्था पनि छैन । बुधबार देवताको अगाडि एक जोडी सिंह स्थापना गरिएको छ ।स्तूपको कुम्भभन्दा माथि हर्मिका रहेको छ । हर्मिकामा एक जोडी आँखा अङ्कित गरिएको छ जसलाई वज्रदृष्टि भनिन्छ । दुई आँखाको बीचमा दायाँतर्फ घुमेको ऊर्णा अङ्कित गरिएको छ । हर्मिकाको माथि हलंपौ राखिएको छैन । हर्मिकाभन्दा माथि चतुष्कोणाकार आकारमा त्रयोदशभुवन राखी आमलक र बाय्‌म्व: सहित गजूर राखिएको छ ।स्तूपको चारैतिर माने राखी शोभा बढाइको छ । स्तूप परिसरमा धर्मधातु मण्डल सहित आठवटा वज्रधातु चैत्य र दुईवटा शिकरकूट चैत्य रहेका छन् । त्यस्तै नाग मानिएको शिला, सरस्वतीको मन्दिर र बत्ती बाल्ने स्तम्भ पनि रहेका छन् ।
monument_assessment: Slightly damaged (minor damages such as minor cracks, plants, missing stones in plinths)
references: Sources and references Sources Vajācārya VS 2056, 55-56

historical_events.event_description: A now lost inscription states that during the reign of Śivasiṃhadeva, acaityalocated near Yampistūpawas renovated. The text of the inscription is published inVajācāryaVS 2056, 55-56.
The inscription names Mevarāma, Hākudeva and Vinhu Simha, disciples of Karmapaṇi Bhikṣu, as donors of the lion statues.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of the Priukhā temple at Aśoka Stūpa
historical_events.event_description: Brahmacarya Bhikṣu Cintāmaṇi of Yampi Vihāra, Rām Bhāro of Konimha and otherguṭhīmembers made the Priukhā temple at the Aśoka Stūpaduring the reign of King Yoganarendra Malla. It is possible that, at that time, the Buddha statues were enshrined in the niches of thestūpa,and that those niches are addressed as the Stūpa temple in the inscription.

historical_events.event_name: Repairs of the stūpa, repair of six caityas and the courtyard paving.
historical_events.event_description: Siṃhavīr Bhāvo, resident of Gaḥchẽ, during the reign of King Rajendra Vikarama Śāhadeva, repaired thestūpaby applyingvajralepaand changing the central pole. He alsorepaired sixcaityasin the courtyard (three at the north-east corner, two at the south-east corner and one at the north-west corner) and paved thestūpacourtyardwithteliyābricks.

Harṣapuṇya Jyoti, resident of Itilhane (Nāga Bāhāḥ), repaired thecaityasituated at the north-east corner (LAL1480-033) and seven additionalcaityasin courtyard. He also constructed a wall surrounding thestūpacourtyard.

historical_events.event_name: Application of cement plaster to the stūpa
historical_events.event_description: Thestūpawas covered with cement plaster. Land was endowed by Lakṣmī Narasiḥma Śākya, resident of Nyākhācuka, for thestūpa'sannual whitewashing.
Consecration of the Dharmadhātu Maṇḍala in front of Akṣobhya shrine.The inscription mentions the donors as Vajrācārya Siddhivajra and family, from Hiraṇyavarṇa Mahāvihāra.
Dhanamāya Maharjan and Kṛṣṇamāya Maharjan donated oil lamps in memory of their ancestors Bābulāl and Hāku Maharjan.
